audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow's defining mechanic — that picking the axe back up resets its cooldown — is absent from both layers. The entry instead invents a 'double-ax rotation' (spikes[1], content.early, whys[1]) that is not what the kit describes.
audit.why: Undertow is one axe on a flat 9s cooldown, and Olaf refunds that entire cooldown by walking over where it landed. That single fact rewrites the trading pattern: the cooldown window the whole entry tells the player to wait for only exists if Olaf cannot retrieve the axe. Fight where the axe is behind him, or step onto the pickup path.
audit.corrected: Undertow is 9s flat — but Olaf picking the axe up resets it outright. Deny the pickup and you get the window; let him walk back over it and there is no window at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] says Olaf 'runs you down freely with true-damage axes', and the full layer's tldr calls his damage '%HP true'.
audit.why: The axes are Undertow: physical damage with an armour shred and a slow. The true damage is Reckless Swing, his E, at 325 range on an 11/10/9/8/7s cooldown — melee, not thrown. And it is flat true damage; nothing in the kit marks it as percent-health. A player told the ranged axes are true damage will build the wrong resistances and misjudge which range band is actually lethal.
audit.corrected: Reckless Swing is the true damage and it only reaches 325. Outside that, his damage is physical and armour works on it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/olaf.json Q Undertow, E Reckless Swing flags trueDamage only

audit.whatIsWrong: Ragnarok is described as unconditional: 'Olaf's R strips all CC', 'CC-immune — your stun won't hold him'.
audit.why: The kit states he is immune to disables 'for as long as he keeps attacking'. The immunity is conditional on him continuing to swing, which means disengaging him off a target is a real counterplay rather than a lost cause. Presented as absolute, it tells the player his entire kit is dead for the duration.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok's immunity holds only while he keeps attacking, and it is 100/90/80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Berserker Rage is never named anywhere, and 'his lifesteal' is treated as a flat constant in four places.
audit.why: Olaf's attack speed AND life steal scale with MISSING health. Tahm Kench's win condition here is attrition, and attrition is exactly what sharpens Olaf — every point of health the player chips off makes the champion he is fighting faster and healthier per swing. This is the reason the extended trade the entry keeps recommending goes badly.
audit.corrected: Berserker Rage pays him more attack speed and life steal the lower he drops — chunking him down is not progress, it is his scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tough It Out is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: It is a shield plus attack speed on 16/15/14/13/12s. The missing-interactions file flags this matchup as shield-absorbs-burst: committing the three-stack cycle into a live Tough It Out spends the whole An Acquired Taste window against a shield.
audit.corrected: Force Tough It Out before you spend three stacks — 16s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says 'Olaf's R is on a long cooldown; track it' and never gives it. No cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: The entry's whole late-game plan is 'punish the five to ten seconds after his R ends' without saying how long you wait for that.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok 100/90/80s. Undertow 9s flat, reset on pickup. Reckless Swing 11/10/9/8/7s at 325. Tough It Out 16/15/14/13/12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and whys[4] give Tahm Kench 'global repositioning with Abyssal Voyage' at level 6.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit. Level 6 gives Devour. whys[4] compounds it by claiming the two ultimates share a cooldown cadence.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour. Abyssal Dive (W) has been the reposition since level 2, 21s at rank 1.

audit.why: 51.99% over 604 games with a chart of Olaf 3 / Skill 3 / Tahm Kench 1 — an early Olaf window resolving into a Tahm Kench item finish. Matches the number and the prose. No change.

audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf's Q Undertow carries a derived 'grounding' flag in the kit file that should not be used.
audit.why: Same parsing artefact as Mordekaiser's Obliterate — the description says he 'throws an axe into the ground', and the deriver read that as grounding. Undertow slows and shreds armour; nothing in it grounds. This is now the second instance of the same bug class in this slice.
audit.corrected: No edit made — flagged so the derivation can be fixed upstream.

edits.after: Undertow slows and shreds armour from 1000, outranging your 900 — and it is only 9s, or no cooldown at all if he collects the axe.

edits.after: Ragnarok makes him immune to disables only while he keeps attacking, and it is 100s at rank 1. His true damage is Reckless Swing at 325, not the axes.

edits.after: Throw Undertow from 1000 to slow and shred your armour, then walk over the axe to reset its 9-second cooldown

edits.after: Undertow bleeds you through Thick Skin's grey health faster than you can idle-heal, and Berserker Rage pays him more life steal the further down you push him.

edits.after: Reckless Swing is true damage at 325 range, so armour and Thick Skin's resistances do nothing about it — three stacks buys a hold, not a kill, and he heals through it.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage gives you global utility but Olaf's R goes up on roughly the same cadence, and he will use it to nullify your Q stun if you try to all-in solo.
edits.after: Level 6 gives you Devour, but Ragnarok is 100s and he will spend it to walk through your stun — though that immunity holds only while he keeps swinging at something.

edits.before: Olaf's axes are his whole level 1-3 kit, but they come with a catch: he needs both to land to do real damage, and you can Q-slow him before the second ax reaches you. Still, his double-ax rotation at level 2 bleeds you fast — Thick Skin's grey health does not regenerate in combat, and Olaf's lifesteal keeps him healthy while he chunks you. Do not try to three-stack and Devour him in these levels; he is not afraid of it yet and his damage trades out ahead. Hug the wave, throw Q to slow an ax, and deny him free extended trades.
edits.after: Undertow is his whole level 1-3 kit, and it comes with a catch worth playing around: it is 9 seconds, but walking over the landed axe refunds the cooldown entirely. Fight on the side where the axe is behind him and that 9 seconds is real; let him stroll back over it and he simply has Undertow again. Thick Skin's grey health does not regenerate in combat, and Berserker Rage hands him more life steal the lower he gets, so chipping him is not progress. Do not spend three stacks in these levels; his damage trades out ahead.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a genuine skill check: Olaf cannot kill you cleanly if you respect the ax slow and keep your grey health converting on cooldown, but you cannot run him down either because his axes outpace your stack-fishing speed. At level 6, your global repositioning with Abyssal Voyage is real, but the dueling math shifts sharply — if Olaf presses his R the moment you land your first Q, the stun never triggers and Devour does nothing; you become a slow-moving frontliner with no lockdown. Play level 6 as a roam threat, not a solo-kill opportunity.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a genuine skill check: Olaf cannot kill you cleanly if you respect the axe slow and keep converting grey health, but you cannot run him down either while he keeps refunding Undertow off the pickup. At level 6 the duelling math shifts sharply — if Olaf presses Ragnarok as you land your first Q, the stun never holds and the three stacks are spent for nothing. The counter is that the immunity lasts only while he keeps attacking, and it is 100 seconds. Play level 6 around that window, not as a solo-kill opportunity.

edits.before: Post-Heartsteel and Sunfire, you are the more durable body in a sustained skirmish and Thick Skin's healing starts absorbing his ax pattern meaningfully. Olaf's R is on a long cooldown; track it, and the moment it expires you have a genuine Devour window to remove him from a fight. Your 2+ items win condition is entirely team-focused: you peel your carry, you absorb axes, and you punish the five to ten seconds after his R ends — you will never truly solo-kill a good Olaf, but you outlast him in a teamfight with correct positioning.
edits.after: Post-Heartsteel and Sunfire, you are the more durable body in a sustained skirmish and Thick Skin's healing starts absorbing Undertow meaningfully. Ragnarok is 100 seconds at rank 1; track it, and the moment it expires three stacks buy a genuine Devour to remove him from a fight. Your 2+ items win condition is entirely team-focused: peel your carry, soak the axes, and punish the seconds after Ragnarok ends. Armour still answers Undertow — it is only Reckless Swing, inside 325 range, that ignores it, so keep that band clear.

notes: Second instance of the kit-file grounding-derivation bug: Olaf's Undertow is tagged 'grounding' because the description says he throws an axe 'into the ground', exactly as Mordekaiser's Obliterate is tagged from 'smashes the ground'. Anyone consuming flags mechanically will generate false grounding advice for both. Worth a pass over every kit whose grounding flag came from a description containing the word 'ground' as a noun. The two content errors most worth propagating champion-wide from this entry: Olaf's true damage is Reckless Swing at 325 range, not his thrown axes (the full layer's tldr even called it '%HP true', which the kit does not support at all), and Undertow's cooldown is refunded on axe pickup, which invalidates every 'wait out his Q cooldown' instruction written without it. The 'Abyssal Voyage' problem reported in tahmkench__mel.json affects content.mid and whys[4] here. No WKM_LINES errors observed for this matchup.
